hints: Apply the Binomial Theorem $(a+b)^5 = \binom{5}{0}a^5 + \binom{5}{1}a^4b + \binom{5}{2}a^3b^2 + \cdots$ with $a = 2$ and $b = -px$.
Calculate each of the first three terms carefully, keeping track of powers of 2 and negative signs.
walkthrough:
Use the Binomial Theorem to expand $(2 - px)^5$ up to the term in $x^2$:
$$(2 - px)^5 = \binom{5}{0}(2)^5 + \binom{5}{1}(2)^4(-px) + \binom{5}{2}(2)^3(-px)^2 + \cdots$$

Evaluate each binomial coefficient and power:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Term 1: } & 1 \times 32 = 32 \\ \text{Term 2: } & 5 \times 16 \times (-px) = -80px \\ \text{Term 3: } & 10 \times 8 \times (p^2 x^2) = 80p^2 x^2 \end{aligned}$$

Combine the first three terms in ascending powers of $x$:
$$32 - 80px + 80p^2 x^2$$

hints: Simplify each coefficient to obtain the first three terms in ascending powers of $x$.
walkthrough:
Use the Binomial Theorem to expand $\left(1 - \frac{x}{2}\right)^4$ up to the term in $x^2$:
$$\left(1 - \frac{x}{2}\right)^4 = \binom{4}{0}(1)^4 + \binom{4}{1}(1)^3\left(-\frac{x}{2}\right) + \binom{4}{2}(1)^2\left(-\frac{x}{2}\right)^2 + \cdots$$

Evaluate each binomial coefficient and simplify:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Term 1: } & 1 \\ \text{Term 2: } & 4 \times \left(-\frac{x}{2}\right) = -2x \\ \text{Term 3: } & 6 \times \left(\frac{x^2}{4}\right) = \frac{3}{2}x^2 \end{aligned}$$

Combine the first three terms in ascending powers of $x$:
$$1 - 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2$$

hints: Multiply the two expansions from parts (a)(i) and (a)(ii): $(32 - 80px + 80p^2 x^2)(1 - 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2)$.
Identify the three pairings of terms that produce an $x^2$ term: $32 \times \frac{3}{2}x^2$, $(-80px) \times (-2x)$, and $80p^2 x^2 \times 1$.
Sum these coefficients, set the total equal to 93, and solve the resulting quadratic equation in $p$.
walkthrough:
Write the product of the two expansions:
$$\left(32 - 80px + 80p^2 x^2 + \cdots\right)\left(1 - 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 + \cdots\right)$$

Collect all terms that produce $x^2$:
$$\begin{aligned} 32 \times \left(\frac{3}{2}x^2\right) &= 48x^2 \\ (-80px) \times (-2x) &= 160px^2 \\ (80p^2 x^2) \times 1 &= 80p^2 x^2 \end{aligned}$$

Equate the total $x^2$ coefficient to $93$ and form a quadratic equation:
$$80p^2 + 160p + 48 = 93 \implies 80p^2 + 160p - 45 = 0$$

Divide through by $5$ and solve the quadratic equation:
$$16p^2 + 32p - 9 = 0 \implies (4p - 1)(4p + 9) = 0$$
$$p = \frac{1}{4} \quad\text{or}\quad p = -\frac{9}{4}$$
